subject.title: Cross-provider fallback should respect provider trust boundaries for images/attachments

question: Should configured cross-provider model fallback imply consent to send user media to the fallback provider, or should OpenClaw add an explicit media trust policy for fallback retries?
rationale: The source path shows a real provider data-boundary gap, but the default affects compatibility, fallback usefulness, and sensitive media disclosure, so automation should not choose it without maintainer intent.

options.title: Add explicit media trust policy
options.body: Preserve existing behavior by default if desired, but add config/docs/runtime checks so users can restrict images and attachments on cross-provider fallback.

options.title: Document configured fallback as full consent
options.body: Keep current forwarding semantics and make the docs clearly state that configured fallbacks may receive prompt text and media.

options.title: Fail closed for cross-provider media
options.body: Strip media on cross-provider fallback by default and require an explicit opt-in for users who want fallback vision behavior.

recommendation.title: Add explicit media trust policy
recommendation.body: Preserve existing behavior by default if desired, but add config/docs/runtime checks so users can restrict images and attachments on cross-provider fallback.

likelyOwner.reason: The current main lines and recent merged refactor for the affected fallback image path are tied to this account, making them the best available routing owner for the maintainer decision.
